body.text: Mañjuśrīparivartāparaparyāyā

children.translated_text: <s>Saptaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom in Seven Hundred Lines)

body.translated_text: Also known as the <s>Mañjuśrīparivarta</s> (Chapter of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>)

body.text: om namo bhagavatyai āryaprajñāpāramitāyai |
body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the noble <s>Āryaprajñāpāramitā</s> (Noble Perfection of Wisdom)

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ paripūrṇena arhadbhikṣusahasreṇa, bodhisattvānāṃ ca mahāsattvānāṃ mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddhānāṃ paripūrṇairdaśabhirbodhisattvaśatasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ sarvairavinivartanīyairanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ | tadyathā - mañjuśriyā ca kumārabhūtena, maitreyeṇa ca, asaṅgapratibhānena ca, anikṣiptadhureṇa ca, evaṃpramukhairdaśabhirbodhisattvaśatasahasraiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s> (Jeta's Grove), in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of monks, a full thousand <s>arhat</s> monks, and together with a full ten hundred thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, who had girded on the great armor, all irreversible from unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Namely: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince, <s>Maitreya</s>, <s>Asaṅgapratibhāna</s>, <s>Anikṣiptadhura</s>—headed by these ten hundred thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto 'ruṇodgatakālasamaye svakādvihārānniṣkramya yena tathāgatavihārastenopasaṃkrāmat | upasaṃkramya vihārasya bahirdvāre sthito 'bhūttathāgatasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya | athāyuṣmānapi śāradvatīputraḥ svakādvihārānniṣkramya yena tathāgatavihārastenopasaṃkrāmadbhagavato darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya | athāyuṣmānapi pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputraḥ, āyuṣmānapi mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ, āyuṣmānapi mahākāśyapaḥ, āyuṣmānapi mahākātyāyanaḥ, āyuṣmānapi mahākauṣṭhilaḥ, anye ca mahāśrāvakāḥ svakasvakebhyo vihārebhyo niṣkramya yena bhagavato vihārastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ, upasaṃkramya ekānte tasthuḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince, at the time of dawn, having gone forth from his own dwelling, approached the dwelling of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, he stood at the outer door of the dwelling to see, venerate, and attend upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> also went forth from his own dwelling and approached the dwelling of the <s>Tathāgata</s> to see, venerate, and attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākauṣṭhila</s>, and other great disciples, having gone forth from their respective dwellings, approached the dwelling of the <s>Bhagavān</s>; having approached, they stood to one side.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānabhikrāntābhikrāntaṃ mahāśrāvakasaṃnipātaṃ viditvā svakādvihārānniṣkramya bahirdvārasyaikānte prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat | niṣadya ca bhagavān jānanneva āyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputramāmantrayate sma - kutastvaṃ śāradvatīputra kalyamevāgatya tathāgatavihāradvāre sthitaḥ? evamukte āyuṣmān śāradvatīputro bhagavantametadavocat - sarvaprathamataraṃ bhagavan mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtastathāgatavihāradvāre sthitaḥ, paścādvayaṃ bhagavantaṃ draṣṭukāmāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing that the great disciples had arrived one after another, went forth from his own dwelling and sat upon the seat prepared to one side of the outer door. Having sat down, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing full well, addressed the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: "From where have you come, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, to stand so early at the door of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s dwelling?" Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "<s>Bhagavan</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince was standing at the door of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s dwelling first of all; we came after, wishing to see the <s>Bhagavān</s>."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān jānanneva mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - satyaṃ kila tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ sarvaprathamataraṃ tathāgatavihāradvāre sthitastathāgatasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya ca? evamukte mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocat - evametat bhagavan, evametat sugata, prathamataramasmyāgataḥ svakādvihārānniṣkramya yena tathāgatavihārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ, upasaṃkramya ekānte sthito bhagavato darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan atṛpto 'haṃ tathāgatasya darśanena vandanena paryupāsanena ca | yadapyahaṃ bhagavan tathāgatamupasaṃkramāmi darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya, tatsarvasattvānāmarthāya | sacedbhagavan (

children.text: ) tathāgato draṣṭavyo vanditavyaḥ paryupāsitavyaḥ, evaṃ draṣṭavyaḥ, evaṃ vanditavyaḥ, evaṃ paryupāsitavyaḥ, yathāhaṃ paśyāmi yathāhaṃ vande yathāhaṃ paryupāse | evaṃ tathāgato dṛṣṭo bhavati vanditaḥ paryupāsitaśca | ahaṃ ca bhagavan sarvasattvānāṃ kṛtaśastathāgataṃ paśyāmi | bhagavānāha - kathaṃ mañjuśrīstathāgato draṣṭavyo yāvat paryupāsitavyaḥ? mañjuśrīrāha - tathatākāreṇa tathāgataṃ paśyāmi avikalpākāreṇa anupalambhayogena, evamanutpādākāreṇa tathāgataṃ paśyāmi, yāvad abhāvākāreṇa tathāgataṃ paśyāmi | na ca tathatā samudāgacchati, evaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi | na tathatā bhavati na vibhavati, evaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi | na tathatā deśasthā na pradeśasthā, evaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi | na tathatā atītā na anāgatā na pratyutpannā, evaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi | na tathatā dvayaprabhāvitā nādvayaprabhāvitā, evaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi | na tathatā saṃkliśyate na vyavadāyate, evaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi | na tathatā utpadyate na nirudhyate, evaṃ tathāgataṃ paśyāmi | evaṃ tathāgato dṛṣṭo bhavati vanditaḥ paryupāsitaśca | evamukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - evaṃ paśyaṃstvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ kiṃ paśyasi? mañjuśrīrāha - evaṃ paśyannahaṃ bhagavan na kiṃcitpaśyāmi | evamahaṃ paśyan na kasyaciddharmasyotpādaṃ paśyāmi na nirodhaṃ paśyāmi ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> should be seen, should be venerated, should be attended upon—thus should he be seen, thus should he be venerated, thus should he be attended upon—as I see him, as I venerate him, as I attend upon him. Thus the <s>Tathāgata</s> is seen, venerated, and attended upon. And I, O Blessed One, see the <s>Tathāgata</s> on behalf of all beings. The Blessed One said: 'How, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, should the <s>Tathāgata</s> be seen, up to attended upon?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Through the mode of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) I see the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through the mode of non-conceptualization, by the method of non-apprehension; thus through the mode of non-arising I see the <s>Tathāgata</s>, up to through the mode of non-existence I see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness) does not come into being—thus I see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. <s>Tathatā</s> neither exists nor ceases to exist—thus I see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. <s>Tathatā</s> is not located in one place nor in another—thus I see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. <s>Tathatā</s> is not past, not future, not present—thus I see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. <s>Tathatā</s> is not produced by duality nor by non-duality—thus I see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. <s>Tathatā</s> is not defiled nor purified—thus I see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. <s>Tathatā</s> does not arise nor cease—thus I see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Thus the <s>Tathāgata</s> is seen, venerated, and attended upon.' When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: 'Seeing thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what do you see?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Seeing thus, Blessed One, I do not see anything at all. Seeing thus, I see neither the arising of any <s>dharma</s> nor its cessation.'

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing full well, addressed <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince: "Is it true, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that you were the very first to stand at the door of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s dwelling to see, venerate, and attend upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>?" Thus addressed, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "It is so, <s>Bhagavan</s>, it is so, <s>Sugata</s>. I came first, having gone forth from my own dwelling and approached the dwelling of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; having approached, I stood to one side to see, venerate, and attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>. For what reason? Indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>, I am insatiable in seeing, venerating, and attending upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Moreover, <s>Bhagavan</s>, when I approach the <s>Tathāgata</s> to see, venerate, and attend upon him, it is for the benefit of all sentient beings. If, <s>Bhagavan</s>—"

body.text: athāyuṣmān śāradvatīputro mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - duṣkarakārakastvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ, yastvaṃ tathāgatamevaṃ paśyasi evaṃ paryupāsse, yasya ca te sarvasattvānāmantike mahāmaitrī pratyupasthitā | na ca te kācitsattvopalabdhiḥ sattvābhiniveśo vā | sarvasattvaparinirvāṇāya cāsi pratipannaḥ | na ca te kaścitsattvābhiniveśaḥ pravartate | sarvasattvānāṃ ca te kṛtaśaḥ saṃnāhaḥ saṃnaddhaḥ | sa cānupalambhayogena yāvadabhāvayogena | evamukte mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ āyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputrametadavocat - evametad bhadanta śāradvatīputra yathā kathayasi | sarvasattvaparinirvāṇāya saṃnāhaścaiṣa saṃnaddhaḥ | na ca me kācit sattvopalabdhirvā sattvābhiniveśo vā | nāyaṃ bhadanta śāradvatīputra saṃnāha evaṃ saṃnaddhaḥ - kathamahaṃ sattvadhātorūnatvaṃ vā kuryāṃ pūrṇatvaṃ vā? sacedbhadanta śāradvatīputra parikalpamupādāya ekaikasmin buddhakṣetre gaṅgānadīvālukopamā buddhā bhagavanto bhaveyuḥ, ekaikaśca tathāgato gaṅgānadīvālukopamān kalpāṃstiṣṭhet sarātriṃdivaṃ ca dharmaṃ deśayamānaḥ, ekaikayā dharmadeśanayā yāvanto gaṅgānadīvālukāsamairbuddhairbhagavadbhiḥ sattvā vinītāḥ, tāvataḥ sattvānekaikastathāgataḥ ekaikayā dharmadeśanayā vinayet, evamapi kṛtvā naiva sattvadhātorūnatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vā prajñāyate | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? sattvaviviktatvāt sattvāsattvād bhadanta śāradvatīputra sattvadhātorna conatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vā prajñāyate ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> spoke thus to the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: 'You are a doer of difficult deeds, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, in that you see the <s>Tathāgata</s> thus and attend upon him thus, and in that great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) toward all beings is present in you, yet you have no apprehension of beings nor attachment to beings. You are set upon the complete <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of all beings, yet no attachment to beings operates in you. You have donned the armor on behalf of all beings, and that by the method of non-apprehension, up to by the method of non-existence.' When this was said, the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s> spoke thus to the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: 'It is so, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, as you say. This armor has been donned for the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of all beings, yet I have no apprehension of beings nor attachment to beings. This armor, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is not donned thus—"How shall I diminish or fill the realm of beings?" If, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, by way of supposition, in each and every <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) there were <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and each <s>Tathāgata</s> were to remain for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> day and night, and by each teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, each <s>Tathāgata</s> were to discipline as many beings as have been disciplined by <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>—even so, neither diminution nor fullness of the realm of beings would be discerned. For what reason? Because of the emptiness of beings, because beings are not beings, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, neither diminution nor fullness of the realm of beings is discerned.'

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān śāradvatīputro mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - yadi mañjuśrīḥ sattvaviviktatvāt sattvāsattvāt sattvadhātornaivonatvaṃ na pūrṇatvaṃ vā prajñāyate, tatkasyedānīṃ bodhimabhisaṃbudhya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyasi? evamukte mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūta āyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputrametadavocat - yadā tāvadbhadanta śāradvatīputra atyantatayā sattvānupalabdhiḥ, tatko 'trābhi

children.text: ) kasya vā dharmaṃ deśayiṣyate? tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi bhadanta śāradvatīputra atyantatayā sarvadharmānupalabdhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) to whom will he teach the <s>Dharma</s>? And for what reason? For, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, there is absolutely no apprehension of any <s>dharmas</s> whatsoever.

body.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> spoke thus to the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: 'If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, because of the emptiness of beings, because beings are not beings, neither diminution nor fullness of the realm of beings is discerned, then for whom will you now teach the <s>Dharma</s> after attaining <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)?' When this was said, the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s> spoke thus to the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: 'When, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, beings are ultimately unapprehended, who then here will attain

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - yadā tāvanmañjuśrīḥ atyantatayā sarvadharmānupalabdhiḥ, tatkimidānīṃ sattvamapi prajñāpayiṣyasi? api ca | sacenmañjuśrīḥ kaścidevaṃ pṛcchet - kiyantaḥ sattvā iti, kiṃ tasya tvaṃ vadeḥ? mañjuśrīrāha - tasyāhaṃ bhagavan evaṃ pṛṣṭa evaṃ vadeyam - yāvanta eva buddhadharmā iti | saced bhagavan punarapi pṛcchet - kiyatpramāṇaḥ sattvadhāturiti, tasyāhaṃ bhagavan evaṃ pṛṣṭa evaṃ vadeyam - yatpramāṇo buddhaviṣayaḥ [iti] ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the young <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: 'If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, there is absolutely no apprehension of any <s>dharmas</s>, will you now designate even a being?' Moreover, '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, if someone were to ask you: How many beings are there? — what would you say to him?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'To one who asks me thus, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I would reply thus: As many as the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. If, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, one were to ask again: Of what measure is the realm of beings (<s>sattvadhātu</s>)? — to one who asks me thus, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I would reply thus: Of the same measure as the domain of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhaviṣaya</s>).'

body.text: bhagavānāha - sacetpunarapi te mañjuśrīḥ kaścidevaṃ pṛcchet - kiṃparyāpannaḥ sattvadhāturiti, kiṃ tasya tvaṃ vadeḥ? mañjuśrīrāha - tasyāhaṃ bhagavan evaṃ pṛṣṭa evaṃ vadeyam - yatparyāpannānutpādācintyatā [iti] ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, someone were to ask you again: Within what is the realm of beings included? — what would you say to him?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'To one who asks me thus, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I would reply thus: It is included within the inconceivability of non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>).'

body.text: bhagavānāha - sacetpunarapi te mañjuśrīḥ kaścidevaṃ pṛcchet - kiṃpratiṣṭhitaḥ sattvadhāturiti, kiṃ tasya tvaṃ vadeḥ? mañjuśrīrāha - tasyāhaṃ bhagavan evaṃ pṛṣṭa evaṃ vadeyam - yatpratiṣṭhito 'nutpādadhātuḥ tatpratiṣṭhitaḥ sattvadhāturiti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, someone were to ask you again: On what is the realm of beings established? — what would you say to him?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'To one who asks me thus, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I would reply thus: On whatever the realm of non-arising (<s>anutpādadhātu</s>) is established, on that the realm of beings is established.'

body.text: bhagavānāha - yasmin samaye tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayasi, tadā kutra pratiṣṭhitāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayasi? mañjuśrīrāha - yasminnahaṃ bhagavan samaye prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayāmi, apratiṣṭhito 'haṃ tasmin samaye prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayāmi ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, at the time when you cultivate <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (the Perfection of Wisdom), where do you stand when cultivating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'At the time, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, when I cultivate <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, I cultivate the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> standing nowhere (<s>apratiṣṭhita</s>).'

body.text: bhagavānāha - apratiṣṭhitasya te mañjuśrīḥ kā prajñāpāramitābhāvanā? mañjuśrīrāha - saiva bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yanna kvacitpratiṣṭhānam ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what kind of cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is it for you who stand nowhere?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that very cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is [the one] which has no standing anywhere.'

body.text: bhagavānāha - yasmin samaye tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayasi, kataratte kuśalamūlaṃ tasmin samaye upacayaṃ gacchati apacayaṃ vā? mañjuśrīrāha - na me bhagavan tasmin samaye kiṃcitkuśalamūlamupacayaṃ gacchati apacayaṃ vā | nāsau prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayati yasya kasyaciddharmasya upacayo vā apacayo vā bhavati | na sā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā veditavyā, yā kasyaciddharmasya upacayāya vā apacayāya vā pratyupasthitā | sā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yā naiva pṛthagjanadharmān jahāti, nāpi buddhadharmānupādatte | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā na kasyaciddharmasyopalambhena pratyupasthitā yaṃ dharmaṃ prajahyādupādadīta vā | sā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yā naiva saṃsāradoṣānupayāti na nirvāṇaguṇān | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan saṃsārameva tāvann samanupaśyāmi, kaḥ punarvādaḥ saṃsāradoṣān | nirvāṇameva tāvannopalabhe, kaḥ punarvādo nirvāṇaguṇān drakṣyāmi | sā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yanna kasyaciddharmasyādānaṃ vā grahaṇaṃ vā niḥsaraṇaṃ vā | sā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yā na kasyaciddharmasya hānirvā vṛddhirvopalabhyate | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi bhagavan anutpādo hīyate vā vardhate vā | (

) yaivaṃ bhagavan bhāvanā, sā prajñāpāramitābhāvanā | sā prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yā na kaṃciddharmamutpādayati vā nirodhayati vā | sā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yā na kasyaciddharmasyonatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vā karoti | yā bhagavan evaṃ bhāvanā, saiva prajñāpāramitābhāvanā | punaraparaṃ bhagavan sā prajñāpāramitabhāvanā yā naivācintyān dharmān prārthayate na prādeśikān | api tu khalu punarbhagavan tadapi na saṃvidyate yatprārthayate, yena prārthayate, yatra prārthayate | evaṃ bhāvanā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā | evaṃ pratyupasthitā ime dharmā agrāḥ ime dharmā hīnā iti | nāpi tān dharmānupalabhate yeṣāṃ dharmāṇāmagratā vā hīnatā vā syāt | evaṃ prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyogamanuyuktaḥ kulaputraḥ sarvadharmān nopalabhate | na bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā kaṃciddharmamagraṃ vā hīnaṃ vā kalpayati | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi bhagavan anutpādasya kiṃcidagraṃ vā hīnaṃ vā, nāpi tathatāyā
bhūtakoṭyāḥ, yāvat sarvadharmāṇāṃ kiṃcidagraṃ vā hīnaṃ vā | evaṃ bhāvanā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā ||
children.translated_text: That cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) which is thus, O Blessed One, is the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). That is the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> which neither produces nor ceases any <s>dharma</s>. That, O Blessed One, is the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> which neither makes any <s>dharma</s> deficient nor complete. That cultivation which is thus, O Blessed One — that itself is the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, O Blessed One, that is the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> which does not seek either inconceivable <s>dharma</s>s or limited ones. Moreover, O Blessed One, that too does not exist — that which seeks, that by which one seeks, that in which one seeks. Such cultivation, O Blessed One, is the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. One does not approach [<s>dharma</s>s] thus: 'these <s>dharma</s>s are supreme; these <s>dharma</s>s are inferior.' Nor does one apprehend those <s>dharma</s>s of which there could be supremacy or inferiority. Thus, a son of good family (<s>kulaputra</s>) devoted to the practice of cultivating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not apprehend any <s>dharma</s>s. The cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, O Blessed One, does not conceive any <s>dharma</s> as supreme or inferior. For what reason? For, O Blessed One, of the unborn (<s>anutpāda</s>) there is nothing supreme or inferior; nor of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), nor of <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality) — up to: of all <s>dharma</s>s there is nothing supreme or inferior. Such cultivation, O Blessed One, is the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, at the time when you cultivate <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, which of your roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) increase or decrease at that time?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that time no root of merit of mine increases or decreases. One who [experiences] increase or decrease of any <s>dharma</s> does not cultivate the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not be understood as one which is directed toward the increase or decrease of any <s>dharma</s>. O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is one which neither abandons the <s>dharmas</s> of ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), nor takes up the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. And for what reason? For, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not directed toward the apprehension of any <s>dharma</s> that one might abandon or take up. O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is one which neither approaches the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) nor the virtues of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (cessation). And for what reason? For, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I do not perceive even <s>saṃsāra</s> itself — how much less its faults! I do not apprehend even <s>nirvāṇa</s> itself — how much less shall I see its virtues! O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is one in which there is no seizing, no grasping, and no escape from any <s>dharma</s>. O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is one in which neither decrease nor increase of any <s>dharma</s> is apprehended. And for what reason? For, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>) neither decreases nor increases. (

body.text: evamukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - na punarmañjuśrīḥ agrā buddhadharmāḥ? mañjuśrīrāha - agrāhyatvādbhagavan agrā buddhadharmāḥ | tatkiṃ punarbhagavan sarvadharmāḥ śūnyā iti tathāgatenābhisaṃbuddhāḥ? bhagavānāha - evametanmañjuśrīḥ śūnyāḥ sarvadharmāstathāgatenābhisaṃbuddhāḥ | mañjuśrīrāha - tatkiṃ punarbhagavan śūnyatāyā agratā vā hīnatā prajñāyate? bhagavānāha - sādhu sādhu mañjuśrīḥ, evametanmañjuśrīḥ yathā kathayasi | na punarmañjuśrīḥ anuttarā buddhadharmāḥ? mañjuśrīrāha - evametadbhagavan anuttarā buddhadharmāḥ | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan teṣvaṇurapi dharmo na saṃvidyate nopalabhyate | na te anuttarā buddhadharmāḥ | punaraparaṃ bhagavan sā prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yā na buddhadharmāṇāmārādhanāya saṃvartate na pṛgjanadharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya saṃvartate | na buddhadharmāṇāṃ vinayitrī, na saṃdhārayitrī | evaṃ bhāvanā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One addressed <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince: 'But, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, are the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s not supreme?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Because they are ungraspable (<s>agrāhya</s>), O Blessed One, the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s are supreme (<s>agra</s>). But has the <s>Tathāgata</s> fully awakened to all <s>dharma</s>s [as being] empty (<s>śūnya</s>)?' The Blessed One said: 'Just so, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has fully awakened to all <s>dharma</s>s as empty.' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'But, O Blessed One, is supremacy or inferiority perceived in emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>)?' The Blessed One said: 'Well said, well said, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>! Just so, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, as you say. But, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, are the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s not unsurpassed (<s>anuttara</s>)?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Just so, O Blessed One — the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s are unsurpassed. For what reason? Because, O Blessed One, not even the slightest <s>dharma</s> exists or is found in them. [Therefore] those <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s are unsurpassed. Furthermore, O Blessed One, that is the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> which does not conduce to the attainment of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, nor conduce to the abandonment of the <s>dharma</s>s of ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). It neither disciplines [one in] the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s nor holds them. Such cultivation, O Blessed One, is the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ sā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā draṣṭavyā yā na kaṃciddharmaṃ cintayati na vijānīte | bhagavānāha - na tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ buddhadharmāṃścintayasi? mañjuśrīrāha - no bhagavan | cintayeyamahaṃ bhagavan buddhadharmān, sacedahaṃ buddhadharmāṇāṃ pariniṣpattiṃ paśyeyam | na bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā kasyaciddharmasya vikalpena pratyupasthitā - ime pṛthagjanadharmāḥ, ime śrāvaka dharmāḥ, ime pratyekabuddhadharmāḥ ime samyaksaṃbuddhadharmā iti | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tameva bhagavan dharmaṃ prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyogamanuyuktaḥ kulaputro nopalabhate, yasyaitān dharmān pṛthagjanadharmān vā nirdiśet, śaikṣadharmān vā nirdiśet, aśaikṣadharmān vā nirdiśet, samyaksaṃbuddhadharmān vā nirdiśet | tānatyantatayā dharmān na samanupaśyāmi | evaṃ bhāvanā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā | na bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyogamanuyuktasya kulaputrasyaivaṃ bhavati - ayaṃ kāmadhātuḥ, ayaṃ rūpadhātuḥ, ayamārūpyadhātuḥ, yāvad ayaṃ nirodhadhāturiti | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi sa bhagavan na kaściddharmaḥ, yo nirodhadharmaṃ samanupaśyati | evaṃ bhāvanā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā veditavyā ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, that cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, O Blessed One, should be understood as that which does not think about nor cognize any <s>dharma</s>. The Blessed One said: 'Do you not think about the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'No, O Blessed One. I would think about the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s, O Blessed One, if I were to see the final accomplishment (<s>pariniṣpatti</s>) of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s. The cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, O Blessed One, does not approach any <s>dharma</s> through conceptualization [in this way]: "these are <s>dharma</s>s of ordinary beings; these are <s>dharma</s>s of hearers (<s>śrāvaka</s>); these are <s>dharma</s>s of solitary awakened ones (<s>pratyekabuddha</s>); these are <s>dharma</s>s of perfectly awakened ones (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>)." For what reason? Because, O Blessed One, the son of good family devoted to the practice of cultivating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not apprehend that very <s>dharma</s> of which one would designate these as <s>dharma</s>s of ordinary beings, or <s>dharma</s>s of learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>), or <s>dharma</s>s of non-learners (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), or <s>dharma</s>s of perfectly awakened ones. I do not perceive those <s>dharma</s>s as ultimately [existing]. Such cultivation, O Blessed One, is the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For the son of good family devoted to the practice of cultivating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, O Blessed One, it is not thus: "this is the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>); this is the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>); this is the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>)" — up to: "this is the realm of cessation (<s>nirodhadhātu</s>)." For what reason? Because, O Blessed One, there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that perceives the cessation of <s>dharma</s>s. Thus should the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> be understood, O Blessed One.

children.text: ) punaraparaṃ bhagavan eṣā sā prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yā na kasyaciddharmasyopakāraṃ vā apakāraṃ vā karoti | na hi bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā buddhadharmāṇāṃ dhātrī, na pṛthagjanadharmāṇāmācchetrī | eṣaiva sā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yā naiva pṛthagjanadharmāṇāṃ nirodhaḥ, na buddhadharmāṇāṃ nirodhaḥ, na buddhadharmāṇāṃ pratilambhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), this is the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) which neither benefits nor harms any <s>dharma</s>. For, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not a nurse of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, nor a cutter-off of <s>pṛthagjana</s>-<s>dharmas</s> (dharmas of ordinary beings). This very cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is one that is neither the cessation of <s>pṛthagjana</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, nor the cessation of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, nor the attainment of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: evamukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - sādhu sādhu mañjuśrīḥ yastvamimamevaṃrūpaṃ gambhīraṃ dharmaṃ deśayasi | sthāpitā te mañjuśrīriyaṃ mudrā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām, ābhimānikānāṃ ca śrāvakāṇām, aupalambhikānāṃ ca bodhisattvayānikānāṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ pratibodhāya | na te mañjuśrīḥ kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā ekabuddhaparyupāsitā bhaviṣyanti naikabuddhāvaropitakuśalamūlāḥ, ye imaṃ gambhīraṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ śrutvā notrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante | api tu khalu punarmañjuśrīḥ atikramya te buddhasahasrāvaropitakuśalamūlā bhaviṣyanti, ye imaṃ gambhīraṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ śrutvā adhimokṣyanti, notrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke thus to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> <s>kumārabhūta</s> (the youthful prince): 'Well done, well done, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that you teach this kind of profound <s>dharma</s>! You have established this seal (<s>mudrā</s>), <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, for the true awakening of <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>mahāsattvas</s>, and of conceited <s>śrāvakas</s>, and of those <s>bodhisattva</s>-vehicle followers who cling to apprehension (<s>upalambha</s>). Those sons or daughters of good family, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, who, having heard this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> teaching, will not be frightened, will not be terrified, will not fall into terror—they will not have attended upon just one <s>Buddha</s>, nor will their wholesome roots have been planted under just one <s>Buddha</s>. Moreover, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, those who, having heard this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> teaching, will have faith in it and will not be frightened, will not be terrified, will not fall into terror—they will have surpassed those whose wholesome roots were planted under thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>.'

body.text: evamukte mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocat - pratibhāti me bhagavan bhūyasyā mātrayā prajñāpāramitānirdeśaḥ | pratibhātu te mañjuśrīḥ, iti bhagavānasyāvocat | mañjuśrīrāha - eṣā sā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yā na kasyaciddharmasya sthitimupalabhate nāsthitim | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? asthitatvātsarvadharmāṇāṃ nopalabhate | eṣaiva sa bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā veditavyā, yā na kasyaciddharmasyādhyālambanāya pratyupasthitā | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan nirālambanāḥ sarvadharmāḥ | evaṃ bhāvanā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> <s>kumārabhūta</s> spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'The teaching of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> occurs to me to an even greater extent, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said to him: 'Let it occur to you, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>.' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'This, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> which does not apprehend the abiding or non-abiding of any <s>dharma</s>. For what reason? Because, due to the non-abiding nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, it does not apprehend [them]. This very cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, should be understood as one that is not present as a support for any <s>dharma</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Bhagavān</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are without support (<s>nirālambana</s>). Thus, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhagavan sā prajñāpāramitābhāvanā draṣṭavyā yatra buddhadharmā api nābhimukhībhavanti kutaḥ punaḥ pratyekabuddhadharmāḥ | nāpi śrāvakadharmā abhimukhībhavanti, kaḥ punarvādaḥ pṛthagjanadharmāṇām ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be seen as that wherein even <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> do not come to the fore—how much less <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>! Nor do <s>śrāvaka</s>-<s>dharmas</s> come to the fore—what need is there to speak of <s>pṛthagjana</s>-<s>dharmas</s> (dharmas of ordinary beings)?

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhagavan sā prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yā(yāṃ?) bhāvanāmāgamya acintyānapi buddhadharmānacintyā buddhadharmā iti na vikalpamāpadyate | seyaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ sarvadharmāvikalpāya draṣṭavyā ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is that by which, having recourse to this cultivation, one does not fall into conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) even regarding the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, [thinking] 'the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> are inconceivable.' This cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, should be seen as [leading to] non-conceptualization of all <s>dharmas</s> for <s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>mahāsattvas</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhagavan sā prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yā(yāṃ?) bhāvanāmāgamya sarvadharmān buddhadharmān paśyati, sarvadharmānacintyadharmān paśyatyasamanupaśyanatayā | bahubuddhaśatasahasraparyupāsitāste bhagavan kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraśca bhaviṣyanti ye imaṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ śrutvā adhimokṣyante nottrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpātsyante ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is that by which, having recourse to this cultivation, one sees all <s>dharmas</s> as <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, sees all <s>dharmas</s> as inconceivable <s>dharmas</s>—by way of non-perception. Those sons and daughters of good family, <s>Bhagavān</s>, who, having heard this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> teaching, will have faith and will not be frightened, will not be terrified, will not fall into terror—they will have attended upon many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhagavan sā prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yāṃ na kaściddharmaḥ saṃkliśyate vā vyavadāyate vā samanupaśyati | evaṃ bhāvanā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā | sā caiṣā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā yā naiva pṛthagjananānātvaṃ karoti, na śrāvakanānātvam, na pratyekabuddhanānātvam, yāvat samyaksaṃbuddhanānātvaṃ ca karoti | eṣā sā bhagavan prajñāpāramitābhāvanā ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is that in which one does not perceive any <s>dharma</s> as being defiled or purified. Thus, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And this, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> which neither creates the differentiation of <s>pṛthagjanas</s> (ordinary beings), nor the differentiation of <s>śrāvakas</s>, nor the differentiation of <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, nor even the differentiation of <s>samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> (perfectly awakened Buddhas). This, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: ) atha khalu bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate sma - kiyantastvayā mañjuśrīḥ tathāgatāḥ paryupāsitāḥ? mañjuśrīrāha - yāvanto bhagavan māyāpuruṣasya cittacaitasikā niruddhāḥ, iyanto mayā bhagavan tathāgatāḥ paryupāsitāḥ | bhagavānāha - na tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ buddhadharmasaṃsthitaḥ? mañjuśrīrāha - kaścitpunarbhagavan sa dharma upalabhyate yo na buddhadharmasaṃsthitaḥ? bhagavānāha - kasya punarmañjuśrīḥ ete buddhadharmāḥ? mañjuśrīrāha - bhagavan tava tāvadete buddhadharmā iti nāma na saṃvidyate nopalabhyate, kutaḥ punaranyeṣāṃ bhaviṣyati?
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince: "How many <s>Tathāgatas</s> have you attended upon, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>?" <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: "As many, <s>Bhagavan</s>, as the mind and mental factors of a magical person (<s>māyāpuruṣa</s>) that have ceased—that many <s>Tathāgatas</s> have I attended upon." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Are you not established in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>?" <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: "Is there, <s>Bhagavan</s>, any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever to be apprehended that is not established in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "To whom, then, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, do these <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> belong?" <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: "<s>Bhagavan</s>, even for you, that which is called '<s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>' is neither found nor apprehended—how much less will it be so for others?"

body.translated_text: [opening parenthesis—textual marker]

body.text: bhagavānāha - prāptā te mañjuśrīrasaṅgatā? mañjuśrīrāha - tadyadā tāvadahaṃ bhagavan na saṅgataiva, tatkiṃ bhūyo 'hamasaṅgatāmanuprāpsyāmi?
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Have you attained non-attachment (<s>asaṅgatā</s>), <s>Mañjuśrī</s>?" <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: "When I am, <s>Bhagavan</s>, already non-attached, how could I again attain non-attachment?"

body.text: bhagavānāha - tatkiṃ niṣaṇṇo 'si mañjuśrīrbodhimaṇḍe? mañjuśrīrāha - bhagavāneva tāvadbodhimaṇḍe na niṣaṇṇaḥ, kathaṃ punarahaṃ niṣatsyāmi bhūtakoṭiṃ pramāṇīkṛtya? bhagavānāha - bhūtakoṭiriti mañjuśrīḥ kasyaitadadhivacanam? mañjuśrīrāha - bhūtakoṭiriti bhagavan satkāyasyaitadadhivacanam | bhagavānāha - kiṃ saṃdhāya mañjuśrīrevaṃ vadasi? mañjuśrīrāha - asanneṣa bhagavan kāyo na satkāyaḥ | naiṣa saṃkrāmati na viṣaṃkrāmati | tenaiṣa kāyo 'satkāya ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Have you then sat upon the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), <s>Mañjuśrī</s>?" <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: "Even the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself has not sat upon the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>—how then could I sit there, taking the ultimate point of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) as measure?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "'<s>Bhūtakoṭi</s>' (the ultimate point of reality), <s>Mañjuśrī</s>—what is this a designation for?" <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: "'<s>Bhūtakoṭi</s>,' <s>Bhagavan</s>, is a designation for <s>satkāya</s> (the embodied self)." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you mean by saying this, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>?" <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: "This body, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is unreal (<s>asan</s>), not a real body (<s>satkāya</s>). It neither passes on nor passes away. Therefore this body is an unreal body (<s>asatkāya</s>)."

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāradvatīputro bhagavantametadavocat - niyatāste bhagavan bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bhaviṣyanti bodhaye, ye imaṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ śrutvā adhimokṣyante notrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti saṃtrāsamāpatsyante ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, <s>Bhagavan</s>, will be determined for awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), who, having heard this exposition of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will have faith in it, will not be frightened, will not be terrified, and will not fall into terror."

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - āsannībhūtāste bhagavan bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bhaviṣyanti bodhaye, ye imaṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ śrutvā adhimokṣyante, notrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? eṣaiva bhagavan paramā bodhiḥ, yaiṣāṃ dharmāṇāmanubodhanā ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, the great being, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, <s>Bhagavan</s>, will be close to awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), who, having heard this exposition of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will have faith in it, will not be frightened, will not be terrified, and will not fall into terror. For what reason? This, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the supreme awakening—namely, the awakening to these <s>dharmas</s>."

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocat - buddhā eva te bhagavan bodhisattvā mahāsattvā draṣṭavyāḥ, ye imaṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ śrutvā adhimokṣyante, notrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? buddha iti paramārthato 'nutpādasyaitadadhivacanam ||
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, <s>Bhagavan</s>, should be regarded as <s>Buddhas</s> themselves, who, having heard this exposition of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will have faith in it, will not be frightened, will not be terrified, and will not fall into terror. For what reason? '<s>Buddha</s>' is ultimately a designation for non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>)."

body.text: atha khalu nirālambā bhaginī bhagavantametadavocat - na te bhagavan bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ pṛthagjanadharmān śrāvakadharmān pratyekabuddhadharmān samyaksaṃbuddhadharmānadhyāmbiṣyante, ye imaṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ śrutvā adhimokṣyante, notrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan nirālambāḥ sarvadharmā asaṃvidyamānatvāt | tenaiṣāmālambanaṃ na saṃvidyate ||
body.translated_text: Then the nun <s>Nirālambā</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, <s>Bhagavan</s>, will not cling to the <s>dharmas</s> of ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), or the <s>dharmas</s> of perfectly awakened ones (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), who, having heard this exposition of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will have faith in it, will not be frightened, will not be terrified, and will not fall into terror. For what reason? Indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are without support (<s>nirālamba</s>), because they are not found to exist. Therefore their support is not found."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputramāmantrayate sma - evametacchāradvatīputra, evametat | niyatāste kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraśca bhaviṣyanti bodhaye, ye imaṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ śrutvā adhimokṣyante, nottrasanti na saṃtrasanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante | avinivartanīyabhūmau tvaṃ (

children.text: ) śāradvatīputra pratiṣṭhitāṃstān kulaputrān kuladuhitaraśca jānīṣva, ye imaṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ śrutvā adhimokṣyante, nottrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante, mūrdhnā ca pratigrahīṣyanti | te te śāradvatīputra paramadānapatayo bhaviṣyanti mahādānapatayo viśiṣṭadānapatayaḥ | te te śāradvatīputra śīlasaṃpannā bhaviṣyanti paramaśīlavantaḥ paramaviśiṣṭaśīlaguṇapathaprāptāḥ, ye imaṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ śrutvā adhimokṣyante, nottrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante | te te śāradvatīputra paramayā kṣāntyā, parameṇa vīryeṇa, paramairdhyānaiḥ, paramayā apratisamayā prajñayā samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti | te te śāradvatīputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvā yāvat sarvakāravaropetena sarvajñajñānena samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti, ye imaṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ śrutvā adhimokṣyante, notrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante ||
children.translated_text: ) <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, know those sons and daughters of good family to be firmly established, who, having heard this exposition of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will have faith in it, will not be frightened, will not be terrified, will not fall into terror, and will accept it upon the crown of their heads. They, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, will be supreme donors, great donors, distinguished donors. They, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, will be endowed with moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), possessing supreme moral conduct, having attained the path of supremely distinguished virtues of moral conduct — those who, having heard this exposition of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will have faith in it, will not be frightened, will not be terrified, will not fall into terror. They, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, will be endowed with supreme patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), supreme vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), supreme meditative concentrations (<s>dhyāna</s>), and supreme, incomparable wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). They, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>, will even be endowed with omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>) possessed of all forms of excellence — those who, having heard this exposition of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will have faith in it, will not be frightened, will not be terrified, will not fall into terror.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: "It is so, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is so. Those sons and daughters of good family will be determined for awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), who, having heard this exposition of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will have faith in it, are not frightened, are not terrified, and will not fall into terror. You, on the irreversible stage (<s>avinivartanīyabhūmi</s>)—"

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhagavan mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūmetadavocat - kaṃ punastvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ arthavaśaṃ saṃpaśyan icchasyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum? mañjuśrīrāha - sacedahaṃ bhagavan bodhaye saṃpratiṣṭheyam, evamahamiccheyamabhisaṃboddhum | nāhaṃ bhagavan bodhiṃ prārthayāmi | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? bodhirevaiṣa yo 'yaṃ mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince: 'Seeing what purpose, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, do you wish to attain unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'If, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I were to take my stand upon <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), then I would wish to attain it. [But] I do not seek <s>bodhi</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>. And for what reason? <s>Bodhi</s> itself is precisely this — <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - sādhu sādhu mañjuśrīḥ, yastvamimānyevaṃrūpāṇi gambhīrāṇi gambhīrāṇi sthānāni nirdiśasi | yathāpi tvaṃ pūrvajinakṛtādhikāro 'nupalambhaciracaritabrahmacaryaḥ | mañjuśrīrāha - labdha eva bhagavan dharmaḥ syāt, yadyahamanupalambhacārī syām ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince: 'Well done, well done, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that you expound such profound, profound points! Indeed, you are one who has performed service under former <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), one who has long practiced the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the mode of non-apprehension.' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> would indeed be apprehended if I were one who practices in the mode of non-apprehension.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - paśyasi tvaṃ mañjuśrīrimāṃ mama śrāvakasaṃpadam? mañjuśrīrāha paśyāmi bhagavan | bhagavānāha - kathaṃ paśyasi? mañjuśrīrāha - tathāhaṃ bhagavan paśyāmi yathā naiva pṛthagjanāna paśyāmi, naiva śaikṣān paśyāmi, naivāśaikṣān paśyāmi | nāpi paśyāmi, nāpi naiva paśyāmi, evaṃ paśyāmi | yannaiva bahūn paśyāmi, nāpyalpakān paśyāmi | yannaiva vinītān paśyāmi, nāpyavinītān paśyāmi ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince: 'Do you see, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, this assembly of my disciples (<s>śrāvakas</s>)?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'I see it, O <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'How do you see it?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I see it thus: I see neither ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), nor those still in training (<s>śaikṣa</s>), nor those beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>). I neither see nor do not see. Thus I see. I see neither many nor few. I see neither the disciplined nor the undisciplined.'

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāradvatīputro mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - yastvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ śrāvakayānikānevaṃ paśyasi, samyaksaṃbuddhayānikān punastvaṃ kathaṃ paśyasi? mañjuśrīrāha - bodhisattva iti bhadanta śāradvatīputra nāma dharmaṃ na samanupaśyāmi, bodhāya saṃprasthita iti nāma dharmaṃ na samanupaśyāmi | bodhāya caratīti nāma dharmaṃ na samanupaśyāmi | abhisaṃbudhyata iti nāma dharmaṃ na samanupaśyāmi | evaṃ bhadanta śāradvatīputra samyaksaṃbuddhayānikān paśyāmi | śāradvatīputra āha - tathāgataṃ punastvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ kathaṃ paśyasi? mañjuśrīrāha - tiṣṭhatu bhadanta śāradvatīputra mahānāgaḥ | mā mahānāgaṃ ghaṭṭaya ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince: 'You, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, see those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle thus; how then do you see those of the vehicle of perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>)?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, I do not perceive any <s>dharma</s> called "<s>bodhisattva</s>." I do not perceive any <s>dharma</s> called "one who has set out for awakening." I do not perceive any <s>dharma</s> called "one who practices toward awakening." I do not perceive any <s>dharma</s> called "one who is awakening." Thus, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, I see those of the vehicle of perfect awakening.' <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said: 'How then, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, do you see the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'Let the Great Elephant rest, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>! Do not disturb the Great Elephant!'

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān śāradvatīputro mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - buddha iti mañjuśrīḥ kasyaitadadhivacanam? mañjuśrīrāha - yatpunarbhadanta śāradvatīputra ucyate ātmeti, kasyaitadadhivacanam? śāradvatīputra āha - anutpādasyaitanmañjuśrīradhivacanaṃ yaduta ātmeti | mañjuśrīrāha - (

children.text: ) evametadbhadanta śāradvatīputra yasyaitadadhivacanamātmeti, tasyaitadadhivacanaṃ buddha iti | api tu bhadanta śāradvatīputra apadādhivacanametad yadidamucyate buddha iti | na hyetadbhadanta śāradvatīputra vācābhirvijñāpayituṃ buddha iti | vāgapi bhadanta śāradvatīputra na sukarā nirūpayitum - iyaṃ vāgiti, kutaḥ punarbuddha iti | api tu bhadanta śāradvatīputra yadevaṃ vadasi - kasyaitadadhivacanaṃ buddha iti, yo na samudāgato notpanno na nirotsyate, yo na kenaciddharmeṇa samanvāgato nāpyatra kiṃcitpadamabhedam, apadasyaitadbhadanta śāradvatīputra adhivacanaṃ yaduta buddha iti | tathāgataṃ bhadanta śāradvatīputra paryeṣitukāmena ātmā paryeṣitavyaḥ | ātmeti bhadanta śāradvatīputra buddhasyaitadadhivacanam | yathā ātmā atyantatayā na saṃvidyate nopalabhyate, tathā buddho 'pyatyantatayā na saṃvidyate nopalabhyate | yathā ātmā na kenaciddharmeṇa vacanīyaḥ, tathā buddho 'pi na kenaciddharmeṇa vacanīyaḥ | yatra na kācitsaṃkhyā, sa ucyate buddha iti | na caitadbhadanta śāradvatīputra sukaramājñātumātmeti yadadhivacanam, evametadbhadanta śāradvatīputra na sukaramājñātuṃ buddha iti yadadhivacanam ||
children.translated_text: 'It is so, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>. That of which "self" is a designation, of that very same thing "<s>Buddha</s>" is a designation. But, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, this is a designation for that which has no designation—namely, what is called "<s>Buddha</s>." For, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is not easy to make known by words what "<s>Buddha</s>" means. Even speech itself, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is not easy to ascertain as "this is speech"—how much less "<s>Buddha</s>"! But, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, since you ask "Of what is '<s>Buddha</s>' a designation?"—that which has not come into being, has not arisen, and will not cease, which is not endowed with any <s>dharma</s>, in which there is no undivided ground whatsoever—of that which has no ground, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, "<s>Buddha</s>" is the designation. One who wishes to seek the <s>Tathāgata</s>, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, should seek the self. "Self," venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is a designation for the <s>Buddha</s>. Just as the self ultimately does not exist and is not apprehended, so too the <s>Buddha</s> ultimately does not exist and is not apprehended. Just as the self cannot be expressed by any <s>dharma</s>, so too the <s>Buddha</s> cannot be expressed by any <s>dharma</s>. Where there is no enumeration whatsoever, that is called "<s>Buddha</s>." And, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, just as it is not easy to understand that of which "self" is the designation, so too, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is not easy to understand that of which "<s>Buddha</s>" is the designation.'

body.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince: '"<s>Buddha</s>" — <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, of what is this a designation?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is called "self" (<s>ātman</s>) — of what is that a designation?' <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said: 'This, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is a designation of non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>) — namely, "self."' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: '(

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāradvatīputro bhagavantametadavocat - nāyaṃ bhagavan mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtastathā deśayati yathā ādikarmikā bodhisattvā ājānīyuḥ | evamukte mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ āyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputrametadavocat - nāhaṃ bhadanta śāradvatīputra tathā deśayāmi yathā kṛtāvino 'pyarhanta ājñāsyanti | nāpyahaṃ tathā deśayāmi yathā kaścidvijñāsyati | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na bodhiḥ kenacidvijñātā, nāpi saṃbuddhā, na dṛṣṭā, na śrutā, na smṛtā, notpāditā, na nirodhitā, noddiṣṭā, nopadeśitā | etāvadeva bhadanta śāradvatīputra yāvatā bodhiḥ | sā ca bodhirna bhāvo nāpyabhāvaḥ | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na bodhyā kiṃcidabhisaṃboddhavyam, nāpi bodhirbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'This youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, Blessed One, does not teach in such a way that beginning <s>bodhisattvas</s> could understand.' When this was said, the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s> spoke thus to the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: 'I do not teach, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, in such a way that even accomplished <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones) would understand. Nor do I teach in such a way that anyone would understand. For what reason? <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) has not been known by anyone, nor has it been fully awakened to, nor seen, nor heard, nor recollected, nor produced, nor ceased, nor indicated, nor taught. This much only, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is <s>bodhi</s>. And that <s>bodhi</s> is neither an existent thing nor a non-existent thing. For what reason? Nothing is to be awakened to by <s>bodhi</s>, nor does <s>bodhi</s> awaken to <s>bodhi</s>.'

body.text: śāradvatīputra āha - na mañjuśrīrbhagavatā dharmadhāturabhisaṃbuddhaḥ? mañjuśrīrāha - na bhadanta śāradvatīputra bhagavatā dharmadhāturabhisaṃbuddhaḥ | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi bhadanta śāradvatīputra dharmadhātureva bhagavān | sacedbhadanta śāradvatīputra bhagavatā dharmadhāturabhisaṃbuddhaḥ syāt, tadyo 'sāvanutpādadhātuḥ sa nirudhyo bhavet | api tu bhadanta śāradvatīputra sa eva dharmadhāturbodhiḥ | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? niḥsattvo hi dharmadhātuḥ | abhāvāḥ sarvadharmā iti bodheradhivacanametat, yo 'sau dharmadhāturiti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? sarvadharmā hyanānātvaṃ buddhaviṣayataḥ | anānātvamiti bhadanta śāradvatīputra avijñaptikaṃ padametat | avijñaptikamiti bhadanta śāradvatīputra naitacchakyaṃ vijñāpayituṃ saṃskṛtatvena vā yāvad asaṃskṛtatvena vā | na tatra kācidvijñaptiḥ, tena tadavijñaptikam | sarvadharmā hi bhadanta śāradvatīputra avijñaptikāḥ | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi sarvadharmāṇāṃ prādurbhāvo nāsti yasmin sthitvā vijñapyeran | ye 'pyamī ānantaryaprasṛtā acintyaprasṛtāḥ, te | ye ca acintyaprasṛtā bhūtaprasṛtāste | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? bhūtamiti bhadanta śāradvatīputra abhedapadametat | ye 'pi acintyadharma

children.text: ) naiva te svargagāminaḥ, na apāyagāminaḥ, na parinirvāṇagāminaḥ | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi acintyaṃ gamanāgamanena pratyupasthitam, yāvat na parinirvāṇaṃ gamanāgamanena pratyupasthitam | ye 'pi bhadanta śāradvatīputra catasṛṣu mūlāpattiṣvavasthitāḥ, amūle te 'vasthitāḥ | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi bhadanta śāradvatīputra anutpādasya mūlaṃ vā agraṃ vā iṣyate | amūlo bhikṣuriti apratiṣṭhitasya bhikṣoretadadhivacanam | utpannamadhikaraṇamiti adhikasamāropasyaitadadhivacanam | adhikasamārope bhadanta sāradvatīputra caran loke dakṣiṇīyo bhavati | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi samaḥ so 'dhikasamāropaḥ | śrāddho bhadanta śāradvatīputra bhikṣurnārhati śraddhādeyaṃ paribhoktum | aśrāddho bhadanta śāradvatīputra bhikṣurarhati śraddhādeyaṃ paribhoktum | kalpito bhadanta śāradvatīputra bhikṣurnārhati śraddhādeyaṃ paribhoktum | akalpiko bhadanta śāradvatīputra bhikṣurarhati śraddhādeyaṃ paribhoktum | asamupahatanetrīko bhikṣurarhan kṣīṇāsrava ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: [continued] They are not bound for heaven, not bound for the lower realms, not bound for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. For what reason? For the inconceivable is not present through coming and going, up to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> is not present through coming and going. Even those, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, who stand in the four root offenses (<s>mūlāpattis</s>)—they stand in the rootless. For what reason? For, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, neither a root nor a tip is admitted for the non-arisen. 'A rootless monk' (<s>amūla bhikṣu</s>)—this is a designation for a monk without foundation (<s>apratiṣṭhita</s>). 'An offense has arisen' (<s>utpannam adhikaraṇam</s>)—this is a designation for superimposition (<s>adhikasamāropa</s>). Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, one who walks in superimposition becomes worthy of offerings in the world. For what reason? For that superimposition is [itself] evenness (<s>sama</s>). Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a faithful monk does not deserve to consume faith-offerings (<s>śraddhādeya</s>). Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a faithless monk deserves to consume faith-offerings. Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a properly constituted (<s>kalpita</s>) monk does not deserve to consume faith-offerings. Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, an unconstituted (<s>akalpika</s>) monk deserves to consume faith-offerings. A monk with undamaged guidance (<s>asamupahatanetrīka</s>) is called an <s>arhat</s> with destroyed <s>āsravas</s> (defilements).

body.translated_text: <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said: 'Has the Blessed One not awakened to the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas), <s>Mañjuśrī</s>?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'No, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the Blessed One has not awakened to the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. For what reason? Because, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the Blessed One is indeed the <s>dharmadhātu</s> itself. If, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the Blessed One had awakened to the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, then that which is the realm of non-arising (<s>anutpādadhātu</s>) would be subject to cessation. But, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that very <s>dharmadhātu</s> is <s>bodhi</s>. For what reason? Because the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is devoid of beings. "All <s>dharmas</s> are non-existent"—this is a designation for <s>bodhi</s>, that which comes to be enumerated as "<s>dharmadhātu</s>." For what reason? Because all <s>dharmas</s> are non-different from the standpoint of the <s>Buddha</s>. "Non-different," venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is an inexpressible term. "Inexpressible," venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>—this cannot be made known either as conditioned or as unconditioned. There is no making-known there; therefore it is inexpressible. All <s>dharmas</s>, venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are inexpressible. For what reason? Because there is no manifestation of all <s>dharmas</s> by abiding in which they could be made known. Those that are proceeding from the infinite are proceeding from the inconceivable. And those proceeding from the inconceivable are proceeding from reality. For what reason? "Reality" (<s>bhūta</s>), venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is an undivided term. Those who are endowed with inconceivable <s>dharmas</s>—'

body.text: śāradvatīputra āha - kiṃ saṃdhāya mañjuśrīrevaṃ vadasi? mañjuśrīrāha - na samatā samupahatā, yā samatā saiva sā netrī | idaṃ saṃdhāya bhadanta śāradvatīputra evaṃ vadāmi - asamupahatanetrīko bhikṣurarhan kṣīṇāsrava ityucyate | anuttīrṇabhaya(bhava?)iti bhadanta śāradvatīputra arhataḥ kṣīṇāsravasyaitadadhivacanam | śāradvatīputra āha - kiṃ saṃdhāya mañjuśrīrevaṃ vadasi? mañjuśrīrāha - aṇūnyapi tasya bhayāni na saṃvidyante | tatkimuttariṣyati? idaṃ saṃdhāya bhadanta śāradvatīputra evaṃ vadāmi - anuttīrṇabhaya iti arhataḥ kṣīṇāsravasyaitadadhivacanamiti ||
body.translated_text: <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said: 'What do you mean by this, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Evenness (<s>samatā</s>) is not damaged; that very evenness is the guidance (<s>netrī</s>). This is what I mean, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, when I say: A monk with undamaged guidance is called an <s>arhat</s> with destroyed <s>āsravas</s>. "One who has not crossed over fear"—Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, this is a designation for an <s>arhat</s> with destroyed <s>āsravas</s>.' <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said: 'What do you mean by this, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Not even the slightest fears exist for him. What then will he cross over? This is what I mean, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, when I say: "One who has not crossed over fear" is a designation for an <s>arhat</s> with destroyed <s>āsravas</s>.'

body.text: śāradvatīputra āha - anutpannakṣāntika iti mañjuśrīḥ kasyaitadadhivacanam? mañjuśrīrāha - yena bhadanta śāradvatīputra aṇurapi dharmo notpāditaḥ, sa ucyate 'nutpannakṣāntika iti ||
body.translated_text: <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said: '"One who has attained the patience of the non-arisen" (<s>anutpannakṣāntika</s>)—<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, for whom is this a designation?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, one by whom not even the slightest <s>dharma</s> has been produced—he is called one who has attained the patience of the non-arisen.'

body.text: śāradvatīputra āha - avinīto bhikṣuriti mañjuśrīḥ kasyaitadadhivacanam? mañjuśrīrāha - avinīto bhikṣuriti bhadanta śāradvatīputra arhataḥ kṣīṇāsravasyaitadadhivacanam | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? avinayo hi vinītaḥ, na vinayo vinītaḥ | idaṃ saṃdhāya bhadanta śāradvatīputra evaṃ vadāmi - avinīto bhikṣuriti arhataḥ kṣīṇāsravasyaitadadhivacanam ||
body.translated_text: <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said: '"An untrained monk" (<s>avinīta bhikṣu</s>)—<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, for whom is this a designation?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: '"An untrained monk," Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is a designation for an <s>arhat</s> with destroyed <s>āsravas</s>. For what reason? For non-training (<s>avinaya</s>) is trained, not training (<s>vinaya</s>) is trained. This is what I mean, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, when I say: "An untrained monk" is a designation for an <s>arhat</s> with destroyed <s>āsravas</s>.'

body.text: śāradvatīputra āha - adhicitte caratīti mañjuśrīḥ kasyaitadadhivacanam? mañjuśrīrāha - adhicitte caratīti bhadanta śāradvatīputra pṛthagjanasyaitadadhivacanam | śāradvatīputra āha - kiṃ saṃdhāya mañjuśrīrevaṃ vadasi? mañjuśrīrāha - tathā hi bhadanta śāradvatīputra so 'dhikaroti ||
body.translated_text: <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said: '"One who walks in the higher mind" (<s>adhicitte carati</s>)—<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, for whom is this a designation?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: '"One who walks in the higher mind," Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is a designation for an ordinary being (<s>pṛthagjana</s>).' <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said: 'What do you mean by this, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'For, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, he super-acts (<s>adhikaroti</s>).'

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān śāradvatīputro mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - sādhu sādhu mañjuśrīḥ, yathā arhan kṣīṇāsravastathā kathayasi | mañjuśrīrāha - evametadbhadanta śāradvatīputra yathā vadasi | kṣīṇāsravo 'smi, na cārhan | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi bhadanta śāradvatīputra kṣīṇā me āsravāḥ ḥrāvakabhūmau vā pratyekabuddhabhūmau vā | anena bhadanta ḥāradvatīputra paryāyeṇa kṣīṇāsravo na cārhan ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> spoke thus to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince: 'Well done, well done, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>! You speak as an <s>arhat</s> with destroyed <s>āsravas</s>.' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'It is so, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, as you say. I am one with destroyed <s>āsravas</s> (<s>kṣīṇāsrava</s>), but not an <s>arhat</s>. For what reason? For, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, my <s>āsravas</s> have been destroyed on the <s>śrāvakabhūmi</s> (śrāvaka-level) and the <s>pratyekabuddhabhūmi</s> (pratyekabuddha-level). By this interpretation, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, I am one with destroyed <s>āsravas</s> but not an <s>arhat</s>.'

children.text: ) atha khalu bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - syānmañjuśrīḥ paryāyo yadbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bodhimaṇḍe niṣaṇṇo 'bhavyo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum? mañjuśrīrāhasyādbhagavan paryāyaḥ yabdodhisattvo mahāsattvo bodhimaṇḍe niṣaṇṇaḥ abhavyo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bodhāvaṇurapi dharmo na saṃvidyate nopalabhyate | tenocyate 'nuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiriti | sā ca bodhiranutpannā | tatra na kaściddharmaḥ saṃvidyate nopalabhyate, yo bodhimaṇḍe niṣīdet, yo vā bodhimabhisaṃbudhyet, yena vā bodhirabhisaṃbudhyeta, yo vā bodhimaṇḍāduttiṣṭhediti | anena bhagavan paryāyeṇa abhavyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bodhimaṇḍe niṣaṇṇo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One spoke thus to the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: 'Could there be a case, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, where a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> seated on the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>) is incapable of attaining unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'There could be such a case, Blessed One, where a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> seated on the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> is incapable of attaining unsurpassed perfect awakening. For what reason? Because in <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), not even an atom of <s>dharma</s> exists or is apprehended. Therefore it is called unsurpassed perfect awakening. And that <s>bodhi</s> is unborn. Therein no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever exists or is apprehended—neither one who would sit on the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>, nor one who would awaken to <s>bodhi</s>, nor that by which <s>bodhi</s> would be awakened to, nor one who would rise from the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>. By this reasoning, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> seated on the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> is incapable of attaining unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - bodhiriti mañjuśrīḥ kasyaitadadhivacanam? mañjuśrīrāha - bodhiriti bhagavan pañcānāmānantaryāṇāmetadadhivacanam | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi bodhiprakṛtikānyeva tāni pañcānantaryāṇi abhāvatvāt | tenaiṣā bodhirānantaryaprakṛtikā, anantaryāṇāmabhisaṃbudhyanā bodhiḥ, na ca pratyakṣībhāvanā sarvadharmeṣu bodhiḥ | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? sarvadharmā hi atyantatayā apratyakṣāḥ | te na kenacidabhisaṃbuddhāḥ, na dṛṣṭāḥ, na jñātāḥ, yāvat na viditāḥ | evameṣā bodhiḥ | api tu khalu punarbhagavan abhimānikaiḥ sthāpitānyetāni abhisaṃbudhāni(ddhā? ), yāvat pratyakṣīkṛtāni ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: '<s>Bodhi</s>—<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, of what is this a designation?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: '<s>Bodhi</s>, Blessed One, is a designation for the five <s>ānantaryas</s> (heinous acts without interval). For what reason? Because those five <s>ānantaryas</s> are by their very nature <s>bodhi</s>, due to their non-existence. Therefore this <s>bodhi</s> is of the nature of the <s>ānantaryas</s>; the awakening to the <s>ānantaryas</s> is <s>bodhi</s>. And <s>bodhi</s> is not the direct perception of all <s>dharmas</s>. For what reason? Because all <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately imperceptible. They have not been awakened to by anyone, not seen, not known, up to not understood. Such is this <s>bodhi</s>. But, Blessed One, it is by the conceited that these awakenings, up to direct perceptions, have been posited.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - kiṃ te mañjuśrīḥ mamāntike evaṃ bhavati - tathāgato me tathāgata iti? mañjuśrīrāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na me bhagavan evaṃ bhavet - tathāgato me tathāgata iti | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? [tathā caiva tathatā ca] yathā ca tathātā, tathā caiṣa tathāgataḥ | tathā hi bhagavan na tathatā tathāgataṃ vijñapayati, nāpi tathāgatastathatāṃ vijñapayati | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan paramārthato 'bhāvā tathatā | abhāvastathāgataḥ | tasmāttarhi bhagavan na me evaṃ bhavati - tathāgato me tathāgata iti | api tu tathāgata iti bhagavan nāmadheyamātrametat | tat kataro 'sau tathāgato yatra me evaṃ bhaviṣyati - tathāgato me tathāgata iti? bhagavānāha - sa(tat?)saṃśayaste mañjuśrīstathāgate? mañjuśrīrāha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan | syādatra me bhagavan saṃśayaḥ, sacet kācittathāgatapariniṣpattiḥ syat, tathāgatotpattirvā tathāgataparinirvāṇaṃ vā ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: 'Is it not the case, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that you think thus in my presence: "The <s>Tathāgata</s> is my <s>Tathāgata</s>"?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'No indeed, Blessed One. For what reason? I do not, Blessed One, think thus: "The <s>Tathāgata</s> is my <s>Tathāgata</s>." For what reason? As is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), so is this <s>Tathāgata</s>. For, Blessed One, <s>tathatā</s> does not make known the <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor does the <s>Tathāgata</s> make known <s>tathatā</s>. For what reason? Because, Blessed One, in the ultimate sense, <s>tathatā</s> is non-existent; the <s>Tathāgata</s> is non-existent. Therefore, Blessed One, I do not think thus: "The <s>Tathāgata</s> is my <s>Tathāgata</s>." Rather, "<s>Tathāgata</s>," Blessed One, is merely a name. Which <s>Tathāgata</s> is it regarding whom I would think: "The <s>Tathāgata</s> is my <s>Tathāgata</s>"?' The Blessed One said: 'Do you then have doubt regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'No indeed, Blessed One. I would have doubt, Blessed One, if there were any accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, or arising of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, or <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - na tava mañjuśrīrevaṃ bhavati - utpannastathāgata iti? mañjuśrīrāha - syānme bhagavan utpannastathāgata iti, saceddharmadhātorutpattiḥ syāt ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: 'Do you not think thus: "The <s>Tathāgata</s> has arisen"?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'I would think, Blessed One, "The <s>Tathāgata</s> has arisen," if the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas) were to arise.'

body.text: bhagavānāha - nādhimucyase tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ gaṅgānadīvālukopamā buddhā bhagavantaḥ parinirvṛtā iti? mañjuśrīrāha - kaścit punarbhagavan ekaviṣayā buddha bhagavanto yadida

children.text: ) bhagavānāha - evametanmañjuśrīḥ, ekaviṣayā buddhā bhagavanto yadidamacintyaviṣayāḥ | mañjuśrīrāha - kaścitpunarbhagavan etarhi tiṣṭhati? bhagavānāha - evametanmañjuśrīḥ | mañjuśrīrāha - tena hi bhagavan ete gaṅgānadīvālukopamā buddhā bhagavanto na parinirvṛtāḥ | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavan ekaviṣayā buddhā bhagavanto yadidamacintyaviṣayāḥ | na ca acintyatā utpadyate nirudhyate vā | tasmādbhagavan bhagavato vā abhisaṃbuddhena (ddhasya?) ye 'pi te anāgate 'dhvani tathagatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bhaviṣyanti, abhisaṃbuddhā eva te | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi acintyatā atītā vā anāgatā vā pratyutpannā vā | tasmādbhagavan vibhramasteṣāṃ lokasaṃniveśaḥ | prapañcayanti te bhagavan lokasaṃniveśaṃ yeṣāmevaṃ bhavati - utpannastathāgato yāvat parinirvāsyati veti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "It is so, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>. All <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, share one domain—namely, the domain of the inconceivable (<s>acintyaviṣaya</s>)." <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: "But does anyone, <s>Bhagavan</s>, abide at this time?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "It is so, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>." <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: "Then, <s>Bhagavan</s>, those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, have not passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. For what reason? Indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>, all <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, share one domain—namely, the domain of the inconceivable. And inconceivability neither arises nor ceases. Therefore, <s>Bhagavan</s>, whether the <s>Bhagavān</s> has fully awakened or those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones who will appear in the future—they are already fully awakened. For what reason? Inconceivability is neither past, nor future, nor present. Therefore, <s>Bhagavan</s>, the world-arrangement is a delusion for them. They elaborate upon the world-arrangement, <s>Bhagavan</s>, who think thus: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> has arisen... up to... will pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.'"

body.text: evamukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - tena hi tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ idaṃ tathāgatācintyam, acintyaṃ niścintyaṃ tathāgatasya vā agrata udāhārairudāhareḥ, avaivartikasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya vā arhato vā kṣīṇāsravasya | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi te śrutvā naivānujñāsyanti, naiva pratikrokṣyanti | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi taccintyamacintyaṃ niścintyam | mañjuśrīrāha - acintyānāṃ niścintyānāṃ bhagavan sarvadharmāṇāṃ ko 'trānujñāsyati vā pratikrokṣyati vā? bhagavānāha - yathaiva mañjuśrīḥ tathāgato niścintyaḥ, tathaiva pṛthagjanā api niścintyāḥ | mañjuśrīrāha - pṛthagjanā api bhagavan tathaiva niścintyāḥ? bhagavānāha - evametanmañjuśrīḥ | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi sarvāṇyacintyāni niścintyāni | mañjuśrīrāha - tatkasmādbhagavānevamāha - yathaiva tathāgato niścintyaḥ, evaṃ pṛthagjanā api niścintyā iti? nanu bhagavan pṛthagjanatvamapi niścintyam | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? niścintyā hi bhagavan sarvadharmāḥ | ye kecidbhagavan parinirvāṇāya prasthitāḥ, vihariṣyante te bhagavan | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? yaiva niścintyatā tadeva parinirvāṇam | tasmāttarhi bhagavan nāsti niścintyatāyāṃ nānātvam | ye 'pi bhagavan evamāhuḥ - ime pṛthagjanadharmāḥ, ime āryadharmā iti, te idaṃ vacanīyāḥ - kalyāṇamitrāṇi tāvatparyupāsadhvam, tataḥ paścājjñāsyatha - ime pṛthagjanadharmāḥ ime āryadharmā iti ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke thus to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince: "Then you, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, should illustrate this inconceivability of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, this inconceivable and unthinkable [teaching], with examples before the <s>Tathāgata</s>, or before an irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) <s>bodhisattva</s> great being, or before an <s>arhat</s> whose defilements are exhausted. For what reason? Because having heard it, they will neither approve nor disapprove. For what reason? Because that which is thinkable is inconceivable and unthinkable." <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: "When all <s>dharmas</s> are inconceivable and unthinkable, <s>Bhagavan</s>, who here will approve or disapprove?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is unthinkable, so too are ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) unthinkable." <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: "Are ordinary beings also thus unthinkable, <s>Bhagavan</s>?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "It is so, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>. For what reason? Because all things are inconceivable and unthinkable." <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: "Then why does the <s>Bhagavān</s> say thus—'Just as the <s>Tathāgata</s> is unthinkable, so too are ordinary beings unthinkable'? Is not the state of being an ordinary being (<s>pṛthagjanatvam</s>) also unthinkable, <s>Bhagavan</s>? For what reason? Indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are unthinkable. Those who have set out for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, <s>Bhagavan</s>, will abide. For what reason? That very unthinkability is itself <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Therefore, <s>Bhagavan</s>, there is no diversity in unthinkability. Those who say, <s>Bhagavan</s>—'these are <s>dharmas</s> of ordinary beings, these are noble <s>dharmas</s>'—they should be told: 'First attend upon good spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>); then you will know which are <s>dharmas</s> of ordinary beings and which are noble <s>dharmas</s>.'"

body.text: evamukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - icchasi tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ tathāgataṃ sarvasattvānāmagryam? mañjuśrīrāha - iccheyamahaṃ bhagavan tathāgataṃ sarvasattvānāmagryam, sacediha kācitsattvapariniṣpattiḥ syāt |
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke thus to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince: "Do you wish, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be supreme among all beings?" <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: "I would wish, <s>Bhagavan</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be supreme among all beings, if there were any real accomplishment of beings here."

body.text: bhagavānāha - icchasi tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ tathāgatamacintyadharmasamanvāgatam? mañjuśrīrāha - iccheyamahaṃ bhagavan tathāgatamacintyadharmasamanvāgatam, sacetkaścidacintyadharmasamanvāgataḥ syāt ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Do you wish, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be endowed with inconceivable <s>dharmas</s>?" <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: "I would wish, <s>Bhagavan</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be endowed with inconceivable <s>dharmas</s>, if there were anyone endowed with inconceivable <s>dharmas</s>."

This realm is established, this realm is unmingled—namely, the inconceivable realm (<s>acintyadhātu</s>). And in that realm, neither the diversity of <s>śrāvakas</s>, up to nor the diversity of ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), is apprehended.

body.text: bhagavānāha - na tvaṃ mañjuśrīrevamicchasi - anuttaraṃ puṇyakṣetraṃ tathāgata iti? mañjuśrīrāha - abhāvatvābhdagavan puṇyakṣetraṃ tathagataḥ, tenaitadanuttaraṃ puṇyakṣetram | yenaitatpuṇyakṣetraṃ nāpuṇyakṣetram, tenaitadanuttaraṃ puṇyakṣetram | api tu khalu punarbhagavan nātra kaściddharmaḥ samudāgacchati na kṣīyate | evaṃ tatpuṇyakṣetram | tatra ca bījaṃ prakṣiptaṃ na vivardhate na parihīyate | bhagavānāha - kiṃ saṃdhāya mañjuśrīrevaṃ vadasi - tatra kṣetre bījamavaropitaṃ na vivardhate na parihīyate iti? mañjuśrīrāha - tathā hi bhagavan acintyaṃ tatkṣetram, evaṃ tatpuṇyakṣetram ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do you not think, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that the <s>Tathāgata</s> is an unsurpassed field of merit (<s>puṇyakṣetra</s>)?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, precisely because of non-existence (<s>abhāvatva</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s> is a field of merit; therefore it is an unsurpassed field of merit. Because this field of merit is not a field of merit, therefore it is an unsurpassed field of merit. Moreover, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, here no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever arises or is exhausted. Such is that field of merit. And a seed planted there neither increases nor diminishes.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'With what intention, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, do you say that a seed planted in that field neither increases nor diminishes?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'For, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that field is inconceivable (<s>acintya</s>); such is that field of merit.'

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāṃ buddhānubhāvena ṣaḍvikāraṃ mahāpṛthivīcālo 'bhūt, ṣoḍaśānāṃ ca bhikṣusahasrāṇāmanupādāyāsravebhyaścittāni vimuktāni, saptānāṃ bhikṣuṇīśatānāṃ trayāṇāṃ copāsakaśatānāṃ catvāriṃśataścopāsikāsahasrāṇāṃ ṣaṣṭeśca kāmāvacarāṇāṃ devakoṭīniyutaśatānāṃ virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurutpannam ||
body.translated_text: Then, at that moment, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, there was a great earthquake with six kinds of trembling, and the minds of sixteen thousand <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) were liberated from the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements) without further grasping. For seven hundred <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), three hundred <s>upāsakas</s> (lay men), forty thousand <s>upāsikās</s> (lay women), and sixty hundred million <s>koṭis</s> of gods of the desire realm (<s>Kāmāvacara</s>), the stainless, immaculate <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (eye of the Dharma) arose regarding the <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānanda utthāyāsanādekāṃsacīvaraṃ prāvṛtya dakṣiṇaṃ jānumāṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - ko bhagavan hetuḥ, kaḥ pratyayo 'sya mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya loke prādurbhāvāya? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmāntamānandametadavocat - ayamānanda puṇyakṣetranirdeśo nāma dharmaparyāyaḥ pūrvakairapi buddhairbhagavadbhirasminneva pṛthivīpradeśe bhāṣitaḥ | ayamānanda hetuḥ, ayaṃ pratyayo 'sya mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya loke prādurbhāvāya ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, extended his palms in salutation toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the cause, what is the condition for the manifestation of this great earthquake in the world?' Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: '<s>Ānanda</s>, this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) called the Exposition of the Field of Merit (<s>Puṇyakṣetranirdeśa</s>) was spoken by former <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, in this very spot on earth. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the cause, this is the condition for the manifestation of this great earthquake in the world.'

body.text: saptaśatikā prajñāpāramitā samāptā ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Saptaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom in Seven Hundred Lines) is concluded.
